Commentary.Commentary: We are back!
... The Run Chase ...

Fair to say that India Under-19 are likely to win this game too but still, the game is not over. Will we see a fight from Uganda Under-19? Or will India Under-19 walk over them? Stay with us to find out.

Angkrish Raghuvanshi is down for a chat. He says that they don't think of any team as minnows and prepare the same way. Adds that the wicket wasn't too different but there was a bit more help for the pacers in the first couple of overs. Says that he feels that he missed out on scoring a double ton but is happy with the team score.

A tough day for Uganda Under-19 in the field. They won the toss and decided to bowl first but after that, nothing went their way. They did get some swing at the start but did not bowl tight lines. They were put under the pump by that one big stand and they could not break that soon enough. All the bowlers had a tough day but Pascal Murungi did manage to get 3 wickets. Their bowlers bowled quite decently in the last few overs, but still, they would be disappointed.

What a fantastic batting show by India Under-19. It was all about two batters though. It was the stand between Raj Angad Bawa and Angkrish Raghuvanshi that has put them in a winning position. The rest of the batters did not have much to do. But Bawa and Raghuvanshi made sure that the others were not needed much. Their 206-run stand got India from a precarious situation to a match-winning one. Raghuvanshi was unlucky to miss out on getting 150 but Bawa crossed that barrier with ease. Still, India Under-19 lost a flurry of wickets towards the end and did not get a blazing finish. They still crossed the 400-run mark though and would be very happy.

Well, after the toss if someone would have told Nishant Sindhu that his team would score over 400, he would have taken it with both hands. That is exactly what has happened after what has been a sensational batting performance by them. This is a massive score and Uganda Under-19 would need to bat out their skins here.

He sticks his right hand out and takes a one-handed stunner.

Drinks. A nice start for India Under-19 but they need a big stand in the middle. Angkrish Raghuvanshi has been solid so far and needs someone to stick around with him for a long time. Uganda Under-19 would hope that the last wicket will provide them with an opening. Raj Angad Bawa is the next batter.

Length ball, on off. Angkrish Raghuvanshi taps it to cover looking for a quick single but is sent back by his partner.
Length ball, outside off. Left alone.

Just past the stumps! Length ball, angling across off. Singh looks to block it with his hands going across but gets the toe end. It drops in front of the stumps and rolls away to the leg side. Single taken.
FOUR! Heaved away! Length ball, on middle and leg. Angkrish Raghuvanshi heaves it over the infield on the leg side. The ball goes over square leg and tickles to the fence.
Full and outside off. Left alone.
Angkrish Raghuvanshi gives this length ball a bit of charge and looks to work it away to the leg side. But he gets the inside edge on the pads.
Full and wide outside off. Another wide as Angkrish Raghuvanshi decides to shoulder his arms to this.
Nicely punched to through covers for a single by Singh.
Short and outside off. Singh looks to cut it away but gets the toe end of the bat.
Full and angling across. Left alone by Harnoor.
Oh, well bowled! Short of a length, lands just outside off and comes back in. Angkrish Raghuvanshi looks to block it from the crease but gets it off the inner half of the bat.
On a length, fifth-stump line and left alone with ease. Nice carry to the keeper.
FOUR! Punished! Short and wide outside off. Angkrish Raghuvanshi thrashes it past covers for a boundary.
Well bowled. Short of a length, landing outside off and it rises. Angkrish Raghuvanshi though rises and works it to backward point.
Miyaji slips it full and on the pads. Angkrish Raghuvanshi looks to flick but gets the edge towards the keeper.
Short of a length, lands way outside off and the swing takes it further away. Left alone and called a wide.
A sharp short one, on the body. Worked past square leg for one.
A maiden then! Length ball, outside off. Left alone with ease.
Nice swing there! Full and outside off. Angkrish Raghuvanshi takes a step down the track and across. He looks to dig it out but it goes past his bat.
Too full and outside off. Punched to short cover.
Another one wide outside off and another easy leave for Angkrish Raghuvanshi.
On a length, but wide enough for Angkrish Raghuvanshi to leave it with ease.
Full again, outside off. Pushed to covers.
Length, on middle. Nicely punched past mid on but the fielder chases it and pulls it back in. The other fielder throws it back in. Three taken.
Juma Miyaji serves a length ball, sixth-stump line. Left alone by Angkrish Raghuvanshi.
Nice and full, on off. Pushed to mid off.
Too full and too wide this time. Left alone with ease.
Well bowled! Back of a length, lands outside off, comes back in and takes off. Left alone by Angkrish Raghuvanshi.
Short and wide outside off. Left alone by Angkrish Raghuvanshi.
Christopher Kidega serves a length ball, on off. Singh blocks it from the crease.
Fuller, on off. Singh goes for the drive but gets the inner half past square leg for a couple.
Full and on the pads. Singh flicks it past mid-wicket and gets a couple.
Well bowled. Length, just outside off. Left alone by Harnoor.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Length and down the leg side. Singh flicks it to the fine leg fence.
On a length, on off. Blocked out.
Who will bowl from the other end? Christopher Kidega it is.
Short of a length, outside off. Left alone. 6 from the first over.
Dropped! That was traveling fast! Short and outside off. Angkrish Raghuvanshi throws his bat at it but gets the outside edge. The ball flies to the man at gully but the fielder drops it.
Well bowled. Juma Miyaji bowls it on a length, outside off. Angkrish Raghuvanshi covers the stumps and leaves it.
On a length, around off. Pushed to cover.
Length and way outside off. Wide called as the batter leaves it alone.
FOUR! Smashed away! Short and wide outside off. Asking to be hit and Angkrish Raghuvanshi cuts it through point for a boundary.
Short and wide outside off. Left alone and called a wide.
On a length, lands outside off and comes back in. Left alone by Angkrish Raghuvanshi though.
Now then. The players have taken the field. Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Harnoor Singh walk out to open for India Under-19. Juma Miyaji has the ball in his hand. Here we go...
We are moments away from the clash as both teams walk out for the national anthems. First, the anthem of Uganda is played followed by that of India.

Uganda Under-19 (Playing XI) - Isaac Ategeka, Brian Asaba, Ronald Lutaaya (In for Ronald Omara), Ronald Opio (In for Mutagana Fahad), Cyrus Kakuru (WK), Juma Miyaji, Joseph Baguma, Christopher Kidega (In for Nuwagaba Edwin), Yunusu Sowobi, Matthew Musinguzi, Pascal Murungi (C).

India Under-19 (Playing XI) - Harnoor Singh, Angkrish Raghuvanshi, Nishant Sindhu (C), Raj Angad Bawa, Kaushal Tambe, Dinesh Bana (WK), Vicky Ostwal, Rajvardhan Hangargekar, Ravi Kumar, Aneeshwar Gautam, Vasu Vats (In for Garv Sangwan).
TOSS - The news from the middle is that Uganda Under-19 have opted to bowl after winning the toss!

India Under-19 have qualified for the next stage with ease by winning their first two games. They would look at this clash as match practice before the next stage and could also give chances to some of their other players. As far as Uganda Under-19 are concerned, they would be looking to get their first win of the competition but that is going to be a difficult task against a strong side from India. Well, regardless, let us hope for a cracking game. Toss and teams in a bit.

Hello and a warm welcome to the clash between India Under-19 and Uganda Under-19 in the ICC Under-19 World Cup. Well, one team is sitting at the top of their group and has already made their way to the next stage of the competition while the other has lost both their games. Will we see India Under-19 walk over to Uganda Under-19 or is an upset on the cards?
